payload.area: NEURONS as a designed/principled unit — existence audit across the whole Fusion workspace (code-fusion/, transformers-fusion/, review-tracking/, .claude/)

findings.fact: CATEGORY (c) — NOTHING. There is NO neuron implementation of any kind anywhere in the workspace. No bio-inspired unit, no hybrid/digital/bio-digital neuron, no spiking neuron, no LIF/integrate-and-fire model, no dendrite, synapse, soma, axon, membrane-potential, refractory, tau/time-constant, STDP, or neuromodulator code. This is a net-new build, not a modification of something existing.
findings.severity: CRITICAL: The entire Req 1 deliverable (per fusion-full-brief.md: neurons carrying BOTH human-neuron AND AI-neuron capabilities, best of both, but DIGITAL, that AI models train on) currently has ZERO code behind it. Any plan step that says 'wire up the existing neurons' will silently build nothing.

findings.fact: Category (a) false-positive #1: NeuralArchitectureSearch is the ONLY symbol in the C++ sources whose name contains 'Neural'. It is a generic architecture/hyperparameter search over a plain struct `Architecture { int layers; int hidden; float score; }` with mutate/evaluate/search methods — no per-unit state, no time dynamics, no signals. Not a neuron.
findings.severity: Medium: name collision. A future grep for 'neuron'/'neural' lands here first and can cause the wrong file to be treated as the neuron host. Duplicated too in install_test/include/quant/agi.h.

findings.fact: Category (a) false-positive #2: 'neural' appears in code-fusion only as an Exa web-search retrieval-mode string literal — `searchType: 'auto' | 'keyword' | 'neural'`. Zero relation to any neuron abstraction.
findings.severity: Low: pure vocabulary collision, but it surfaces in workspace greps and will waste a cycle during implementation.

findings.fact: Category (b) generic neural-net vocabulary and the only remaining 'neur' hits: bench prose about real ANN weight distributions ('Real neural weights are locally correlated', 'Real neural weights are sparse'), a NAS label, a test string 'transformers are powerful neural network architectures', and `has_vnni` = 'Vector Neural Network Instructions' (an Intel INT8 GEMM ISA flag). None is a neuron unit.
findings.severity: Low: must be classified out honestly so it is never reported as partial neuron coverage.

findings.fact: Category (b) generic 'LIF'-adjacent false-negative risk: `leaky` in the sources is ONLY the LeakyReLU activation string ('leaky_relu' nonlinearity param, and sqrt(2/(1+a^2)) init gain). It is NOT leaky integrate-and-fire.
findings.severity: Medium: 'leaky' is the single most likely term to be mis-scored as a spiking-neuron match in any automated coverage check. It is a ReLU variant.

findings.fact: Category (b) generic: every 'consolidat*' hit is memory/batch management, never sleep-like biological consolidation. `MemorySystem::consolidate()` merges memory entries whose cosine similarity > 0.95 by averaging them.
findings.severity: Medium: the name is suggestive of the biological mechanism but the physics is unrelated (a dedup/average pass, not an offline replay-and-strengthen process).

findings.fact: REUSABLE BUILDING BLOCK — the strongest existing 'neuron-like' state container is WorldModel's StateMemoryEntry: a state with a float importance_weight, access_count and last_accessed, stored in a bounded deque (max 10000), plus update_importance_weights(), consolidate_memory(), and a Transition struct carrying reward, predicted_reward and prediction_error.
findings.severity: High: this is the closest thing to a per-unit importance/decay/trace state that already exists and is the natural host surface for a hybrid neuron. Missing pieces vs a real neuron: no time constant, no threshold, no spike, no refractory period, no local plasticity rule.

findings.fact: REUSABLE BUILDING BLOCK — a real two-timescale stability/plasticity controller exists and is wired into training. StabilityPlasticityParams {forgetting_weight, current_lr_factor, stability_lr_factor, plasticity_lr_factor, forgetting_threshold}; when forgetting exceeds threshold it scales stability up and plasticity down, clamps both to [0.1, 5.0], and returns an effective learning rate.
findings.severity: High: a genuine adaptive-plasticity rule already exists — the module-level analogue of meta-plasticity. A hybrid neuron should reuse this rather than inventing a second one. Note it is gated on QUANT_INFERNO_ENABLED and falls back to pass-through.

findings.fact: REUSABLE BUILDING BLOCK — ECC / Elastic Weight Consolidation is fully implemented: ECCState { fisher_diagonal, anchor_weights } with update_fisher(gradients, n, alpha), update_anchor(weights, n) and regularize(current_weights, n, lambda). The Fisher diagonal is exactly a per-parameter importance score, which is the canonical 'synaptic consolidation' primitive.
findings.severity: High: per-parameter importance + anchoring is the single most directly reusable piece for neuron-level consolidation. Also present in install_test/include/quant/continual_engine.h.

findings.fact: REUSABLE BUILDING BLOCK — Fisher-weighted importance sampling with exponential decay already exists in the replay buffer: CompressedReplayEntry.fisher_importance, plus update_importance(float decay_rate) and importance_resample(). This is a working importance-decay mechanism.
findings.severity: Medium: gives a decay_rate-driven importance trace to copy for a neuron's weight trace, though it operates on replay samples, not units.

findings.fact: REUSABLE BUILDING BLOCK — full reward / prediction-error / curiosity stack: RewardModel (score_pair, reward_loss, compute_abstention_reward, importance_factor=8.0), CuriosityDrivenExplorer::intrinsic_reward(state) with a visited_states_ history, plus WorldModelStats.avg_prediction_error and avg_reward_prediction_error. WorldModel also exposes predict_with_uncertainty and UncertaintyEstimate splitting epistemic vs aleatoric.
findings.severity: High: this supplies the dopamine-analogue (reward prediction error) and the novelty/curiosity signal a digital neuron would need for local credit assignment, without a global backward pass.

findings.fact: REUSABLE BUILDING BLOCK — gating already exists at two levels: (1) MoE gating/importance, `const float* importance` passed into a MoE enhance path; (2) the flywheel's hard pass gate. Neither is a per-unit neural gate, but the MoE router is the natural place a 'which unit fires' decision would live.
findings.severity: Medium: the gating primitive exists but is routing-shaped, not membrane-threshold-shaped.

findings.fact: The AGI subsystem that would host a neuron abstraction is real and substantial: agi.cpp 44.2K, agi_extended.cpp 34.0K, agi_flywheel.cpp 102.9K, agi_guardrails.cpp 11.2K, meta_cognition.cpp 30.7K, multi_agent.cpp 27.3K, self_eval.cpp 31.5K, world_model.cpp 25.0K, plus agi.h 19.3K. Host classes present: SelfMonitor, MemorySystem, PlanningEngine, ToolUse, EvaluationHarness, Flywheel, CapabilityAmplifier, CuriosityDrivenExplorer, HPOptimizer, ContinuousLearner, KnowledgeDistillation.
findings.severity: High: confirms an excellent scaffolding exists to hang a neuron type on (namespace quant::agi, existing headers, build wiring) — the absence is of the neuron itself, not of a place to put it.

findings.fact: Everything AGI-related is duplicated into install_test/include/quant/ (agi.h, world_model.h, continual_engine.h, simd_math.h, etc.). Any neuron work must land in BOTH trees or the install_test copy drifts.
findings.severity: Medium: a real, easy-to-miss duplication trap; the two trees already contain divergent filenames (sops_integration.h vs inferno_integration.h).

findings.fact: code-fusion/packages contains no neuron-analogue, and no reward/prediction-error/gating machinery to reuse. Its matches for reward/gate/importance are all unrelated infrastructure: verification 'proof gate' (gatePassed), workflow worker cancellation gates, and token-meter/ralph test strings.
findings.line: 60, 114-115, 134, 184-197 (proof gate); cf/, context/, goal/, core/, llm/, workflow/ also checked
findings.severity: Medium: correctly rules out code-fusion as a source of hybrid-neuron building blocks. Per the brief code-fusion is 'bas harness hai' — a harness, not the neural substrate. The neuron must live in transformers-fusion.

payload.notes:
VERDICT: Category (c) — NOTHING. There is no implemented neuron-like unit anywhere in the Fusion workspace. This is stated plainly and is the headline answer.

METHOD. I swept the entire tree with rg --no-ignore --hidden (the repo has ignore files that silently hid results on the first pass — notably code-fusion/.rgignore and a large .gitignore chain, so a default grep gives FALSE CLEAN results here; this must be repeated with --no-ignore by anyone re-checking). Term battery run case-insensitively: neuron/neurons/neuronal/neurone, dendrite, synapse, action-potential, spike/spiking, SNN, membrane, leaky, integrate-and-fire, LIF, tau, time-constant, refractory, neuromodulat, dopamine, serotonin, plasticity, hebbian, homeostat, sleep, consolidation, meta-plasticity, soma, axon, digital-neuron, hybrid-neuron, dual-neuron, bio-digital, neuro-engine, neuron-engine, NPU, neuromorphic, brain-inspired, brain-like. Also swept every doc/notes/archive/review-tracking location: code-fusion/docs, code-fusion/.agents, code-fusion/archive, code-fusion/.claude, review-tracking/, and the session memory dir.

THE ONE REAL 'neuron' HIT workspace-wide is prose in an unrelated news-source list (code-fusion/skills/ai-news-collectors/references/sources.md). Excluding skills/ and vendor/, the whole workspace has ZERO occurrences of 'neuron'. Every other 'neur' hit is one of three collisions I verified by reading: NeuralArchitectureSearch (generic NAS), Exa's 'neural' search mode, and ANN-prose/'Vector Neural Network Instructions'.

THE THREE CATEGORIES, CLEANLY SEPARATED:
(a) Real neuron implementation: NONE. No file, no class, no struct, no function.
(b) Generic NN vocabulary misread as neuron-like: NeuralArchitectureSearch (agi.h:378 — the only 'Neural' symbol in C++), leaky_relu (init.h:23,26 — mistakenly lava-adjacent to leaky-integrate-and-fire), consolidate (agi_extended.cpp:507, world_model.cpp:630, production.h:129 — memory/batch, not sleep), NPU (backend.cpp:84,1429,2118; gpu_compute_openvino.cpp:62-277; gpu_compute_zdnn.h:22 — it is a hardware target, NOT Neural Processing Unit code; several of those comments exist precisely to say NPU work is NOT really running), stability/plasticity (inferno_integration.h:152-193 — real but module-level, not per-unit), 'neural' search mode.
(c) Nothing: everything else.

A SHARP DISTINCTION WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. The workspace is rich in MODULE-LEVEL analogues of the mechanisms a neuron needs, but has no UNIT-LEVEL implementation of any of them. Concretely, the following neuron primitives exist only at the wrong granularity: plasticity (a scalar LR factor applied to a whole trainer, inferno_integration.h:164 / continual_trainer.cpp:152), importance (a per-parameter Fisher diagonal, continual_engine.h:86-100, or a per-memory-entry weight, world_model.h:87-91 — never a per-unit weight trace), decay (update_importance(decay_rate), continual_engine.h:54, over replay samples), reward/prediction-error (RewardModel and WorldModelStats, real and usable, reward.h:18 / world_model.h:96-97), gating (MoE router, moe_enhance.h:13). What is absent entirely: any notion of TIME inside a unit (no tau, no time constant, no timestep), any THRESHOLD or spike, any refractory period, any per-unit local update rule, any soma-like state integration. A hybrid bio-digital neuron therefore needs a NEW unit type whose per-unit state sits on top of these existing signals — it cannot be assembled by renaming or exposing what is there.

HONEST CAVEAT ON THE REQUIREMENT ITSELF. The brief's framing ('neuron carrying BOTH human-neuron and AI-neuron capabilities, best performer of both, but DIGITAL, that models then train on') is a legitimate engineering direction, but note the transcript it derives from explicitly says the biological side is NOT fully understood — 'we ourselves still don't have a complete answer' to how memory forms, how one experience permanently changes the brain, how regions synchronize, how chemicals alter attention and learning. So there is no known complete spec to implement against; the implementable subset is the one whose primitives already exist here: per-unit importance/decay, thresholded activation, local plasticity driven by reward prediction error, and offline consolidation. Anyone planning this should scope it to that subset rather than implying the biological half can be faithfully reproduced.

NO INVENTED CONTENT. I did not create, modify, or write any file. I found no neuron and am reporting none. Note also that the neuron requirement has no in-repo home at all — no spec, header, TODO or issue in either repo — so the first real deliverable is a written design that both trees can be built from, and it must land in transformers-fusion (namespace quant::agi) AND its install_test/include/quant duplicate, since code-fusion is the harness and holds no neural substrate.

KEY PATHS: c:/Users/thaku/Workspaces/fusion/transformers-fusion/include/quant/{agi.h, world_model.h, continual_engine.h, inferno_integration.h, reward.h, hpo_nas.h}; c:/Users/thaku/Workspaces/fusion/transformers-fusion/src/agi/{agi_extended.cpp, world_model.cpp, agi_flywheel.cpp}; c:/Users/thaku/Workspaces/fusion/transformers-fusion/install_test/include/quant/ (duplicate tree); c:/Users/thaku/Workspaces/fusion/code-fusion/packages/ (checked, no analogue); c:/Users/thaku/.claude/projects/c--Users-thaku-Workspaces-fusion/memory/{fusion-full-brief.md, fusion-transcript-2-neurons-j-rsi.md, fusion-pending-work-neurons-astra.md} (the only place the requirement is recorded).

payload.area: AREA A (provider adapter & thinking preservation) + AREA B (context/compaction package & world-model question) — read-only exploration of c:\Users\thaku\Workspaces\fusion\code-fusion

findings.fact: The literal phrase 'thinking-preservation' has ZERO occurrences anywhere in the workspace (case-insensitive, all extensions). The earlier scan's single 'hit' was a false positive — packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/README.md discusses *replay state* and *reasoning efforts*, never 'thinking-preservation'. Consequently the premise 'the 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 pattern' has no referent: 'arc-agi' / 'arc agi' also has ZERO hits workspace-wide.
findings.severity: Any plan that starts from 'extend the existing thinking-preservation code' will find nothing to extend — this is a net-new subsystem, and the 'ARC-AGI-3 / 99.9%' claim is unsupported by this codebase.

findings.fact: packages/llm/ contains exactly 5 packages: llm (seam + `LlmRuntime` + content/stream vocabulary), llm-deepseek, llm-pi-ai, llm-retry (retry policy, not an adapter), token-meter. Only TWO production provider adapters exist: llm-deepseek and llm-pi-ai. Plus a test-only replay adapter at packages/test-support/llm-replay.
findings.severity: Reporting 'llm, llm-deepseek, llm-pi-ai and others' as four+ adapters overstates the surface; the real answer is two production adapters, and any new reasoning feature must be built into exactly two wire implementations.

findings.fact: llm-pi-ai speaks pi-ai's normalized multi-provider protocol over pi-ai ('@earendil-works/pi-ai'), covering openai-completions, openai-responses, azure-openai-responses, openai-codex-responses, anthropic-messages, bedrock-converse-stream plus hand-declared OpenAI-compatible gateways. Request mapping: packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/context.ts `toPiContext`/`textOnlyContext` -> pi-ai `Context {systemPrompt, messages, tools}`. Response mapping: src/stream.ts `toStreamChunks` (pi-ai `thinking_start`/`thinking_delta`/`thinking_end` -> `block-start`/`reasoning-delta`/`block-end` at lines 148,151,154).
findings.severity: pi-ai is the only adapter that sees native thinking/signature events; assuming DeepSeek's flat `reasoning_content` text model generalizes would break signature-carrying providers.

findings.fact: llm-deepseek speaks DeepSeek chat-completions directly (`fetch` + SSE via eventsource-parser) with no third-party protocol lib. Request mapping: packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/serialize.ts (harness `Message[]` -> `WireMessage[]`). Response mapping: src/translate.ts (SSE deltas -> StreamChunks).
findings.severity: The two adapters have structurally different request/response serializers, so any cross-adapter reasoning feature needs two independent implementations plus a seam-level contract.

findings.fact: Reasoning IS a first-class durable content block in the seam: `interface ReasoningBlock { type: 'reasoning'; text: string }` registered in `ContentBlockMap`, and `reasoning-delta` is a StreamChunk variant. There is NO field on ReasoningBlock for signatures, effort, confidence, or provenance — it is a bare text string.
findings.severity: Provider thinking-signatures cannot be stored in content — they live only in the separate opaque `replayState`; anything wanting durable reasoning metadata beyond raw text must extend this block type (the file explicitly requires 'adapter, UI, and compaction support' for a new block type).

findings.fact: DeepSeek reasoning passback IS implemented: `serializeAssistant` joins every `type==='reasoning'` block's text and emits it as `reasoning_content` on the wire for every reasoning-carrying turn (not only tool-call turns). Inbound, `translate.ts:132` reads `delta.reasoning_content` and opens a reasoning block. Text-only — DeepSeek has no signature concept in this code.
findings.severity: For the DeepSeek route, reasoning is ALREADY carried across turns; building a 'thinking preservation' layer there would duplicate existing behaviour.

findings.fact: pi-ai signature-preserving replay IS implemented: `toPiReplayState` projects the response into a versioned `ReplayEnvelope` carrying per-block `thinkingSignature`, `redacted`, and `thoughtSignature` (tool-call thought) plus response-level `api`/`provider`/`model`/`responseId`/`responseModel`/`stopReason`. `replayedAssistant` recombines durable harness `ReasoningBlock.text` with those signatures on a later request; `toPiAssistant` falls back to `foreignAssistant` (which maps reasoning -> `{type:'thinking', thinking: block.text}` with `api:'cf-foreign'`) on any validation failure, emitting an `INVALID_REPLAY_STATE` diagnostic via `onReplayDegrade`.
findings.severity: This is the single most advanced reasoning-carry mechanism in the repo and the closest thing to the requested 'pattern'. A plan that treats it as absent would rebuild what exists; a plan that treats it as universal would ignore its three hard limits below.

findings.fact: Replay state is scoped to ONE adapter instance: `LlmRuntime.forAdapter()` strips `source.replayState` from any assistant message whose historical `provider` route is not currently owned by the same adapter instance receiving the request. Changing adapter instance, provider, or model therefore degrades that message to foreign provider-neutral conversion (signatures dropped, reasoning TEXT retained).
findings.severity: Provider signatures are NOT portable across model/provider switches — the most common real operation (switching models mid-session) silently drops them. Only the reasoning text survives.

findings.fact: Replay metadata is block-count-coupled: if `envelope.blocks.length !== message.content.length`, or a per-entry type mismatches, `BlockAssembler` discards the WHOLE envelope, and `replayedAssistant` throws `INVALID_REPLAY_STATE` for the whole message. Any block-level edit (prune, truncate, user edit, UI rewrite) to an assistant message invalidates its signature replay.
findings.severity: Any future reasoning-preservation feature that mutates assistant content (e.g. compaction that edits rather than shadows) will silently destroy replay fidelity for that whole message.

findings.fact: There is NO mechanism anywhere in code-fusion that carries reasoning across context compaction. Compaction's summarizer projects its output to text-only via `summaryText()` (`blocks.filter(b => b.type === 'text')`), and the package README states it explicitly: 'Only returned text enters the checkpoint, excluding reasoning and tool calls that would leak private reasoning or create an orphaned call.' A reasoning-only summarizer output is rejected as an error ('summarization produced no text summary content').
findings.line: 168-171 (summary + emptiness check), 217-224 (summaryText text-only filter); README.md:16; tests/compaction-basic.spec.ts:1393
findings.severity: THIS IS THE CENTRAL GAP. Reasoning survives across turns but is destroyed the moment its region is compacted. Any 'thinking preservation' work must intercept compaction, not adapters.

findings.fact: The compaction summarizer itself IS shown the reasoning: `buildSummarizationInput` maps each shadowed surface seq through `session.deriveEventMessage()`, which returns the full `assistant/message` including reasoning blocks. So reasoning reaches the summarizer as input context — it is only the OUTPUT that is text-restricted.
findings.severity: Reasoning can influence the checkpoint's content indirectly, but never verbatim. Building 'preserve reasoning verbatim' means changing the replacement message, not the summarization request.

findings.fact: History is built as `session.deriveMessages()` (full current surface) on every step; `deriveEventMessage` returns `event.data.message` verbatim for `user/message`, `assistant/message`, `tool/result` — no filtering of reasoning. The agent loop stores the assembled message via `createAssistantMessage({content: assembler.blocks(), source: {provider, model, replayState?}})` appended as `assistant/message` with `surfaceOp:'append'` and `sourceEventSeqs` citing the raw `assistant/chunk` events.
findings.severity: Cross-turn reasoning preservation is IMPLEMENTED end-to-end up to the durable log; do not describe it as missing.

findings.fact: All reasoning is dropped from cross-session snapshots by design: session-reference's projection 'keeps only direct-user user/message, assistant text, and user/message checkpoints' and explicitly excludes 'Shadowed pre-compaction events, tools, reasoning'.
findings.severity: Even where reasoning is durable in the source log, one whole context subsystem strips it — reasoning never transfers between sessions.

findings.fact: Reasoning is excluded from the full-text session index: `blockText()` returns `[]` for `case 'reasoning'`, so reasoning text is never searchable — despite being durably stored in the log.
findings.severity: Durable-but-unfindable: any 'retrieve prior reasoning' feature built on ctx.sessionQuery will find nothing.

findings.fact: Reasoning effort is per-conversation durable config, not adaptive: `LlmCallConfig.reasoningEffort` is logged in `request/header`, restored for later steps only when it was NOT an adapter default (`adapterDefaults.reasoningEffort !== true`), and may be replaced each step by the `agent/request` waterfall. `LlmRuntime.resolveCallConfig` rejects unsupported explicit effort ids with `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT` before network I/O rather than clamping. There is NO feedback loop that adjusts effort from outcomes.
findings.severity: Effort selection is static/user-driven; 'learn which effort works' requires a new mechanism.

findings.fact: Reasoning IS priced (it counts toward the token budget that drives compaction): `estimateContent` case 'reasoning' charges `ceil(text.length/4) + 4`. So a reasoning-heavy turn actively triggers compaction, and its own reasoning is what gets destroyed first.
findings.severity: Reasoning both consumes the budget and loses its budget — a self-defeating loop on long reasoning models (the compaction README line 162 also notes 'hidden reasoning tokens can consume' the summarizer's 8192-token cap).

findings.fact: UI rendering of reasoning is implemented: chat shows a collapsible 'Think' disclosure row (`ReasoningRow`) driven from `AssistantMarkdown`; the Trajectory view builds `thinkingDetail` from reasoning blocks and shows `usage.reasoning` token counts.
findings.severity: Human-visible reasoning already exists; only the model-visible path loses it at compaction.

findings.fact: Compaction strategy (IMPLEMENTED): head-anchored range selection that walks the priced surface backwards accumulating tokens until `retainTokens` (default = floor(window * 0.16)), backs off to a tool-pairing-balanced cut, and returns `{start: surfaceNodes[0], end: surfaceNodes[keepFromIdx-1]}` — i.e. compact EVERYTHING older than the retained tail. Pressure threshold default = floor(window * 0.8). Overflow recovery bypasses retention entirely and attempts 'one maximal balanced head reduction'.
findings.severity: Retained tail = verbatim (reasoning intact); everything else = replaced by one text checkpoint. Reading '0.16 retained' as '16% is preserved' understates it: the older 84% is wholesale replaced, not thinned.

findings.fact: Nothing is permanently destroyed in the durable log: cf-session is an append-only event log ('A Session is the append-only source of truth'), surface `replace` operations only rewrite the model-visible projection and cite `sourceEventSeqs` back to the originals; the only content-rewriting path is the tool-result pruner's single-node `tool/result` rewrite. No delete/truncate/GC/rewrite API exists on Session. Human transcript deliberately uses `isAppendSurfaceEvent` (append-origin events) so replaced ranges remain visible to the user.
findings.severity: Reasoning is recoverable from the LOG but not from the MODEL VIEW. Distinguish these sharply: durable = preserved; model-visible = lost after compaction.

findings.fact: The loss is nevertheless effectively permanent for the model, because later compactions re-summarize from the *surface* (not the log): `prepareCompaction` builds input from `selection.shadowedSeqs` which are current-surface seqs, and a prior checkpoint has already shadowed them. There is no path that reads the pre-compaction log back into a request.
findings.severity: After N compactions the reasoning is unrecoverable by any model-visible route. A 'reasoning memory' store would need to be written at append time, not recovered later.

findings.fact: Context eviction outside compaction is limited to tool output: `packages/spill/` replaces oversized tool results with a bounded preview + a locator to session-scoped local files (content kept on disk, model can re-read it). `packages/compaction/compaction-tool-result-pruner/` head/tail-slices only `type==='text'` blocks in `tool/result` nodes and passes non-text blocks (including reasoning) through untouched. Neither touches assistant reasoning.
findings.severity: There is NO global truncation/eviction policy — compaction is the only assistant-history shrinker, and it is the reasoning-destructive one.

findings.fact: packages/context/ holds NO reasoning or compaction logic — it is six unrelated context injectors: agent-instructions (AGENTS.md chain injection), file-reference + file-reference-local (@path grammar + local fuzzy index), session-reference (cross-session snapshots, reasoning-excluded), time-context (zoned timestamp), tmux-context (pane layout). None participates in compaction or reasoning retention.
findings.severity: The task's pairing of 'context package' with 'compaction package' is architecturally wrong: they are independent capability families with no shared code.

findings.fact: World model: code-fusion has NONE. Workspace-wide search for world|worldModel|world_model|world-model|dynamics|transition|simulate finds, for real model semantics, only: transformers-fusion/include/quant/world_model.h (namespace quant::agi; `struct Transition {WorldState state; std::string action; WorldState next_state; float reward; float predicted_reward; float prediction_error;}`; `class WorldModel { WorldModel(Model*, int64_t state_dim=64, int64_t ensemble_size=5); ... float simulate_step(...); std::vector<Tensor> plan(int64_t horizon); ...}`), transformers-fusion/src/agi/world_model.cpp, transformers-fusion/CMakeLists.txt:314, transformers-fusion/include/quant/agi.h:6/362/542-545, transformers-fusion/tests/test_wave7_missing.cpp:31-66, transformers-fusion/tests/test_agi_safety.cpp:129. Every other hit is unrelated (scroll fixtures, cordis lifecycle 'transitions', Landlock 'world-proof', gen-config-catalog's type-resolution `World`, simulation stubs in tests).
findings.severity: The world model exists ONLY in the C++ engine. Treating code-fusion as if it had one — or as if a bridge existed — is wrong: there is no FFI/napi binding anywhere (native/ contains only landlock-run; python/ contains only sdk/sdk-runtime).

findings.fact: Learning from an environment: ABSENT in the mounted harness. The only environment feedback channel is tool results inside the in-session history (`executeToolCalls` -> `tool/result` -> surface -> next request). Nothing updates weights, prompts, policies, or routing from outcomes. Skill/instruction 'learning' is human-authored files discovered from the filesystem (skill-filesystem, agent-instructions), not learned.
findings.severity: The harness has no learning loop at all — an RL/world-model plan cannot 'extend' anything; every layer (reward signal, state/transition model, durable parameter store, applier) must be created.

findings.fact: The ONLY outcome-driven adaptation in the repo is `@origin-ai/cf-mad` (packages/cf), and it is NOT part of the npm workspace: root `workspaces` is `packages/*/*`, which does not match the single-level `packages/cf`. `node_modules/@origin-ai/cf` is a stale symlink to `/c/Users/thaku/Workspaces/code-fusion/apps/cli`. Scope was read-only (Grep/Glob/Read via shell); no files modified. Absolute paths are under c:\Users\thaku\Workspaces\fusion\ unless stated.

Three corrections to the task's premises, stated first because they change what should be built:
1. `thinking-preservation` has zero occurrences workspace-wide — the earlier scan's "one hit" in packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/README.md is a false positive (that file discusses *replay state* and *reasoning efforts*).
2. `arc-agi` / `99.9%` also have zero occurrences. The "ARC-AGI-3 pattern" has no referent in this codebase.
3. packages/context/ and packages/compaction/ are unrelated capability families with no shared code; only compaction handles history shrinkage.

Answering the seven questions directly:

(1) Search terms. `adapter`/`provider-adapter` resolve to exactly two production adapters plus the seam. `thinking`/`reasoning` resolve to a first-class `ReasoningBlock` in the seam, two adapter serializers, the token meter, the UI, and compaction's *exclusion* of it. `extended_thinking` has zero hits; `reasoningEffort`/`chain-of-thought` hit config/docs/skills only; `scratchpad` has zero hits.

(2) packages/llm/ inventory and per-adapter protocol + reasoning carry — see findings 2-8. Short version: llm-deepseek carries reasoning as verbatim `reasoning_content` text; llm-pi-ai carries reasoning text PLUS per-block thinking/tool signatures in an opaque `replayState`; llm-retry and token-meter are consumers, not adapters; llm-replay (test-support) is test-only.

(3)/(4) Conversation history and reasoning preservation across turns and compaction — see findings 10-19. Across turns: IMPLEMENTED and verbatim (surface -> deriveMessages -> adapter serialization). Across compaction: ABSENT by explicit design (text-only checkpoint). Cross-adapter and cross-session: partial/stripped.

(5) Compaction strategy — see findings 20-23. Head-anchored replace of everything older than a 16%-of-window retained tail; 80%-of-window pressure threshold; summary must shrink or the whole transaction is rolled back. Nothing is deleted from the durable log; everything older than the retained tail is removed from the model-visible surface. The tool-result pruner rewrites single tool-result text in place (the one content-mutating path); spill relocates oversized tool output to files with a locator.

(6) World model — see findings 24-28. Absent from code-fusion; exists only in transformers-fusion C++ (namespace quant::agi, Transition/reward/simulate_step/plan) with no bridge (native/ = landlock-run only; python/ = sdk only). The nearest JS analogue is the unmounted, non-workspace @origin-ai/cf-mad ModelRouter running average; packages/mad/* are 7 unmounted stub packages.

(7) Can the harness learn from an environment? No — it observes tool results into history and nothing more; no weights, prompts, policies, or routing update from outcomes, and nothing persists across sessions except human-authored workspace files. What would have to be added: (a) a reward/success signal source and a place to score it (compaction/token-meter measure cost, ctx.telemetry only records); (b) a world-model capability family following the seam pattern (docs/capability-seams.md:429, packages/compaction/README.md:5-8) — 3 packages + ctx key + a `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml` mount; (c) durable learned state, which must be a new event type added to packages/core/session/src/known-event-types.ts plus an `SessionEventMap` declaration merge (the precedent is packages/compaction/compaction/src/types.ts:9-69) — note the log is append-only with no update verb, so state is last-write-wins-by-new-event; (d) an applier — the only candidate in-tree is the unmounted MAD ModelRouter, which itself needs workspace wiring (`workspaces` is `packages/*/*`, which does not match `packages/cf`) and persistence; (e) optionally, a native bridge if the C++ quant::agi::WorldModel is to be reused rather than reimplemented.

Method: Glob/Grep/Bash only, no Read on large files; keyword sweeps on attention|transformerblock|transformerconfig|rmsnorm|softmax|kv_?cache|flashattn|lm_head|ffn|moe|router|expert|gating|projector|layernorm|linear|embedding|positional|rope|rotary|qkv|causal|unembed|cross.?attn plus explicit class/struct-declaration greps and ::forward/::apply/::route definition greps. All call-site claims verified by tree-wide grep (e.g. AttentionResidual has exactly 6 hits, all its own declaration/definition/comment; moe_quantized_test_*.cpp have zero external callers).

Key structural facts the parent needs before planning the replacement:
1. There is no single transformer to replace. There are 6-8 coordinate implementations across src/model, src/multimodal, src/inference and engines/, no two of which are copies. The anchor src/model/transformer.cpp:295 Attention::forward is the most important one but covers only the DenseModel training path.
2. The two highest-fan-out couplings are NOT in transformer.cpp: (a) 14 files re-enumerate the traditional layer tensors by hand for optimizers/FSDP/TP/Zero (trainer_core.cpp:36, moe_trainer.cpp:104, trainer_rl.cpp:526, fsdp.cpp:91, tensor_parallelism.cpp:290, ddp.cpp, pipeline.cpp, distributed.cpp, etc.); (b) 13 files hardcode the on-disk weight-name schema (layers.N.attention.q_proj.weight etc). Both need a deliberate interface decision before any code moves, or the replacement trains a silent subset and cannot load checkpoints.
3. Training vs inference take different attention code: Attention::forward branches on AutogradEngine::enabled() into autograd_functions.cpp:17 ScaledDotProductAttentionFunction (training, graph) versus flash_attention_forward / a hand-rolled causal softmax (inference). Replacing one branch only is a classic trap.
4. engines/trainer/dense is trainer-only (52 of 70 files have zero transformer hits; max is 11 and those hits are 'linear'/'nonlinearity' gain strings in init.cpp). Only 4 dense files are in scope: mtp.{h,cpp}, lora.{h,cpp}, init.cpp, and precision/distill consumers. The other 66 are indifferent to the model swap.
5. engines/trainer/moe and engines/trainer/multimodal/moe ARE in scope at the layer level (layers.h MoELayer has its own router; mm_router.h is a second multimodal router; mm_experts.h a second expert pool), not merely trainer wrappers.
6. Build reality: all 35 engines/trainer/dense .cpp and all engines/trainer/{moe,multimodal} .cpp ARE listed in CMakeLists.txt (verified zero unlisted), so the untracked tree is genuinely built, not dormant. But 80 files under engines/trainer are untracked in git and 10 files are modified — commit before a wholesale rewrite.
7. Prior art to read before designing: the retired-name block at src/model/transformer.cpp:669-685 names three previously-removed attention variants (LatentKVAttention, GatedDeltaAttention, TransFormersFusionDeltaAttention) plus a retired transformer.cpp-local MultiTokenPredictionHead, and transformer.h:116-118 explicitly says the Cender/ formula (Phase 19-23, owner-gated) is the intended replacement and standard Attention remains the sole mixer until it proves parity. That comment is the project's own statement of the replacement contract.
